clue.text: Less than wholly grown up, a politician being complimentary

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is cut away

parts.note: a grown-up person is an adult
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A not-quite-adult politician is being flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than wholly' trims ADULT to ADUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory praise is fawning flattery, so it is complimentary in excess.

clue.text: Daughter encountering rascal? I may act as an anchor

definitions.text: I may act as an anchor

parts.note: a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A daughter meets a rascal, who might then steady her like an anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue is a sea anchor, a cone of canvas trailed to slow a boat.

clue.text: Behold — container has nothing in it that can help soothe skin!

parts.note: lo is an old word for behold

indicators.note: something is placed within the container just named, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a tin is a container
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Look, a jar with nothing in it, yet it can soothe the skin!
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a cream or liquid rubbed in to calm or heal skin.

clue.text: Theologian at home — pi mask's blown apart!

indicators.note: being blown to pieces scatters the letters of these words into a new order

explanation.surface: A theologian at home finds his pious mask shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all thirteen letters of AT HOME PI MASKS, the 's being 'is' and so a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas a Kempis was the medieval German monk who wrote The Imitation of Christ, a theological classic.

clue.text: Book shows what struggling tennis player may have to do

definitions.meaning: to book a table is to make a booking in advance

definitions.text: what struggling tennis player may have to do
definitions.meaning: a player whose first serve fails must serve again

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-SERVE, to serve again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book; to re-serve is to serve once more after a fault.

clue.text: Dog of small height you brought up in sports field?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for a sports field

parts.note: a ground is a sports field

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A short dog you raised on a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' reads the archaic 'you' from the bottom upward, giving EY; 'in' then sets it with the height letter inside the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is a breed of slender racing dog.

clue.text: Arrive outside club accompanied by one very pugnacious

indicators.note: the word for arrive goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a bat is a club used in games
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone turns up outside a nightclub with a companion, spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Combative and pugnacious both describe someone eager to fight or argue.

clue.text: Hill — not all of it suffered a landslide?

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England
a part of something is not all of it

explanation.surface: Only part of a hill gave way in a landslip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fell apart collapsed or disintegrated, as ground does in a landslide.

clue.text: Sitting by stream is English poet

parts.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: An English poet sits beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was the English war poet who wrote The Soldier.

clue.text: Nothing in tub by river building close to the water

indicators.note: the nothing letter is placed within the word for tub

parts.note: a bath is a tub
O looks like zero, nothing
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: An empty bathtub beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A boathouse is a shed by a river or lake for storing boats.

clue.text: See 19
Maybe 'ave a graft on top to try and be posh?

definitions.meaning: a hair transplant puts on hairs, said with the h dropped as in 'ave
to give oneself airs is to act grandly

explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of 'ave signals that 'hairs' loses its h too.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means behaving in a pretentious, superior manner.

clue.text: Finish by Italian river in drowsy period of recovery?

indicators.note: the word for finish is placed right beside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
to stop is to finish

explanation.surface: Ending up beside an Italian river in a sleepy convalescence.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-op means just after a surgical operation, when a patient is often groggy and recovering.

clue.text: Carol, enchanting woman inside, is changing

indicators.note: the woman's word is placed within the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a witch casts enchantments

explanation.surface: Carol, with a charming lady inside her, is changing.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name but is a verb, to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching is swapping one thing for another, so it means changing.

clue.text: Man and pal try to mess about in unrestrained fashion

indicators.note: messing about jumbles these words' letters together

explanation.surface: A man and his friend try fooling around wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampantly means unchecked and wild, without restraint.

clue.text: Teach posh fools to make disparaging remark

indicators.note: to fool with something is to mess it about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Teaching posh idiots prompts a snide comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap shot is an unfair, belittling criticism.

clue.text: Companion going off fruit and veg

indicators.note: leaving means the companion's letters are removed from the fruit

parts.note: a peach is a fruit
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A companion loses interest in fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a common green vegetable.

clue.text: Party regularly ignored peer

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is skipped

explanation.surface: A party is routinely snubbed by a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a noble but is the verb to look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To pry is to peer nosily into others' affairs.

clue.text: Equip a fighting force

definitions.meaning: a branch of the military is one of its ...

explanation.definitionFit: Arm means supply with weapons, and also a branch of the armed services.

clue.text: It might be a sign of brighter times ahead

definitions.text: It might be a sign of brighter times ahead

parts.words: It might be a sign of brighter times ahead
parts.note: the sun icon on a forecast map promises sunnier days, not better fortunes

explanation.walkthrough: Brighter times sounds like hope, but means sunshine forecast on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecast maps show icons such as a sun for fine conditions to come.

clue.text: As motorist crushed dog crossing middle of lane

indicators.note: the dog's name stretches across the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: Rover is a traditional dog's name

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A driver flattened a dog as it crossed the lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who ran over something hit it and passed across it with the car.

clue.text: Root crop available with month returning

indicators.note: coming back means the month's name is read backwards

parts.note: May is a month

explanation.surface: A root crop on offer as a month comes round again.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a starchy tuber grown as a staple crop in the tropics.

clue.text: See 4
Path to get new tile

indicators.note: making something new remakes the letters in another order

explanation.surface: A garden path gets a fresh paving tile.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is dated slang for a hat, and a top hat is a tall formal one.

clue.text: Is poet exceptional man of many letters?

indicators.note: out of the ordinary suggests the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the poet a remarkable man of letters?
explanation.walkthrough: Man of letters suggests a writer; a postie is British slang for a postman.
explanation.definitionFit: A postie, British slang for a postman, delivers many letters daily.

clue.text: Producing publication about one's relatives

indicators.note: the publication's word goes around the relatives

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Bringing out a magazine about one's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something is creating or producing it.

clue.text: Lewd fellow giving sly look — chap's half hidden

indicators.note: the half of the word is tucked within the look

parts.note: a leer is a sly, lustful look

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: A lewd man casts a sly glance, half his face concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first two letters of CHAP, and 'hidden' tucks them into the sly look; the surface makes 'hidden' sound like a concealed face.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecher is a man given to lewd lust.

clue.text: Exploded, being old-fashioned about public school

indicators.note: the old-fashioned word goes around the school

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: It blew up because it was behind the times at a public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous fee-paying school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Detonated means set off or exploded, as a bomb is.

clue.text: A little house and a comfy one, really!

parts.note: HO is a short form of house
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: A small house and a cosy one, truly!
explanation.definitionFit: Honest! as an exclamation insists on truth, just as Really! does.

clue.text: Draw attention to big tummy in insulting remark

indicators.note: the tummy word goes inside the remark

parts.note: a slight is an insult
a pot is a pot belly

explanation.surface: Highlight a paunch in a rude comment.
explanation.definitionFit: To spotlight something is to focus attention on it.

clue.text: Christmas duck being demolished by boy sailor

indicators.note: the duck is knocked out of the Christmas word

parts.note: Noel is Christmas
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A Christmas duck is destroyed by a young sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is cricket's word for a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was Britain's most celebrated admiral.

clue.text: Basildon blonde perhaps showing legs — Rex is excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A blonde from Basildon displays her legs and Rex gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a town in Essex; the Essex girl is a British stereotype of a brash young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essex girl is a stereotype, and Basildon is an Essex town, so a blonde from there exemplifies it.
